business.title: Designing and simulating a real-time SCADA-based monitoring system for the Tis-Abay II hydroelectric power plant
business.description: Automation is a method for monitoring and regulating systems, enhancing work quality by utilizing control systems, intelligent electronic devices, instrumentation, and new communication technologies. In the Tis-Abay II hydropower plant, the previous SCADA (H9000) has an outdated operating system and is currently not functional. Nowadays, due to the failure of the SCADA in the plant, all tasks are executed manually, which decreases the willingness of the operators to work day-to-day. The study allows real-time data acquisition, control, and monitoring through the Simatic WinCC Runtime Advanced SCADA within the TIA Portal software for the Tis-Abay II hydroelectric power station. In the operational control segment, the control programs were developed, and a human-machine interface (HMI) was designed for configuration changes, parameter settings, and status indications. The new SCADA system was simulated and validated. The simulation results enable users to get historical data points across various time intervals, alarm operators for predefined events as per the identified real-time, and allow for insightful analysis and trend view identification when the generator runs at an output power of 36 MW, with a terminal voltage of 10.5 KV, a current of 2083.8 A, and reactive power of 13.4 MVAR.=

science.title: Combined effects of a novel reduced graphene oxide-enriched diesel-hazelnut biodiesel-tetrahydrofuran blend on combustion and emission characteristics of a compression ignition engine
science.description: The gradual exhaustion of fossil fuel reserves and the enforcement of stricter emission regulations have driven the search for sustainable and environmentally friendly alternative fuels for compression-ignition engines. In this study, the effects of the combined use of hazelnut biodiesel, tetrahydrofuran (THF), and reduced graphene oxide (rGO) nanoparticles on combustion characteristics, engine performance, and exhaust emissions were experimentally investigated in a diesel engine. Pure diesel, biodiesel–diesel blends, THF-containing blends, and nanofuel blends enriched with 50, 100, and 150 ppm rGO nanoparticles were tested under three engine loads (11, 16.5, and 22 Nm). Combustion analysis was performed using in-cylinder pressure data. The indicated mean effective pressure (IMEP), thermal efficiency (TE), specific fuel consumption (SFC), ringing intensity, combustion duration, maximum pressure rise rate, cyclic variations, and CO, CO₂, HC, and NOx emissions were evaluated. The experimental results showed differences in combustion characteristics, engine performance, and exhaust emissions among the tested fuel blends. Among the tested nanofuels, the highest IMEP increase reached 21.79% at low engine load, and cyclic variations were reduced through improving combustion stability. In addition, CO and NOx emissions decreased by up to 29.41% and 13.09%, respectively. The rGO-containing fuel blends reduced HC emissions by up to 14.9% at high engine load and increased thermal efficiency by up to 3.92%. These findings indicate that fuel blends containing hazelnut biodiesel, THF, and rGO nanoparticles can contribute to improved engine performance and reduced harmful exhaust emissions under the investigated operating conditions.
